To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rate of economic growth and the redistribution of income matter in poverty reduction.

(1) the poverty elasticity of economic growth is higher in the Philippines than in other developing countries, (2) the poverty elasticity is higher for the bottom 30% than for the bottom 40%, (3) the poverty elasticity increases as income distribution becomes more equal, and (4) the poverty elasticity for the bottom 20% is higher in the regions with a higher share of agriculture in the economy.
the Philippines is a country where the rich are growing faster than the poor, the poor have been growing faster than the rich, and the rich have been growing faster in the last few years.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What are the relationships among poverty, growth, and inequality? How do the different economic sectors contribute to the poverty rate in the regions? What is the role of income inequality in poverty reduction? How can the government address poverty in the country?
understanding the relationship between economic growth, poverty, and inequality, and the role of regional economic growth and inequality in the poverty reduction process in the Philippines.
how the growth rate and income distribution affect poverty in the Philippines, particularly the relationship between economic growth and poverty.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
growth and redistribution of income are both important in poverty reduction.
economic growth and income distribution are both important for poverty reduction.
economic growth is the most important factor for poverty reduction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a given growth rate, a more unequal society would have a higher poverty elasticity than a less unequal one.
, while the Philippines has been growing, the growth has not been inclusive and the benefits of growth have not been shared equally.
the Philippines needs to grow faster to reduce poverty, but it is more important to make sure that this growth is inclusive and not only benefiting the rich.
The main takeaway from our work is that
growth is not enough for poverty reduction, and that the government should also pursue policies that promote a more equal income distribution.
the government should focus on policies that will increase the productivity of labor in the agricultural sector and improve the quality of life of the poor.
growth is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for poverty reduction.
